title: Ulysses by Elevator Repair Service at The Public #ulysses #elevatorre...
transcript: I tried so hard to lock in for this, and even though I failed miserably, I don't even think that's why I didn't enjoy it. On the heels of their epic, full-day production of Gatz, Elevator Repair Service is back at The Public with an adaptation of a notoriously convoluted novel by James Joyce. Compared to Gatz, this one has a shorter (though not short) run time and covers a much longer book. Initially set up like a seminar or a literature class with the cast sitting at large desks in formal wear, this context becomes progressively less relevant, to the point where you may forget about it completely. In fairness, it seems like the novel itself is written in a way that would make a theatrical throughline impossible to effectively maintain. I still enjoyed the performances, the visual direction, and the types of stylistic choices that I recognized from Gatz, but I found this production lacking a strong framing device or point of view. I appreciated the big swings here, but overall it felt like a miss, mostly due to the source material. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
